findings.title: Keep-current lets a previously approved CRM plan and its paid authorization survive a target contract change, against R2 05:121 (which the plan itself quotes)
findings.reproduction: Plan line 44 quotes 05:121: "Unaffected CLEAN artifacts may remain valid under the equivalence procedure, but a previously approved CRM plan does not automatically survive." The same line then defines "supersede the old contract iff no plan is bound OR some non-terminal bound plan is affected; otherwise the old contract stays current (equivalence)". Line 20 adds the OK test "a newer contract with no lost bound value leaves the paid authorization executable". Target contracts exist only for HUBSPOT and SALESFORCE work (M3: CLEAN is vacuous), so the equivalence branch applies exactly to the CRM plans R2 excludes. A HUBSPOT project confirms a newer contract that adds a required field on an object the plan does not write and changes a picklist the plan does not use: the old contract stays current, and the APPROVED plan and its ACTIVE authorization run on without revalidation. That is the automatic survival 05:121 forbids. My r1 ADV-3 acceptance criterion ("stay executable or are re-bound") allowed this branch: reviewer omission.
findings.acceptance_criterion: In CRM modes, a confirmed newer contract whose body differs from the current one in anything but observedAt supersedes it; every approved plan bound to it stops being executable until it is revalidated against the newer contract (the included repair) or refunded. Equivalence is allowed only for byte-identical objects (re-observation) or for CLEAN artifacts, each case with its R2 citation.
findings.failing_test: T3 "R2-026: OK a newer HUBSPOT contract that changes an object the plan does not bind supersedes the old one; ExecuteProject on the paid authorization answers TARGET_STALE, nothing charged, includedPaths offered"; plus "R2-026: OK a re-observation with identical objects keeps the authorization executable".

scope.why: r1 ADV-3 acceptance criterion to be corrected

findings.title: CMD019 reads the bound plans with no lock that the plan writers take, and plans born after a keep-current decision are never judged; the claim that a plan bound while B decides is seen is false
findings.reproduction: Lock trace on 99266f52. Actor B (CMD019 rev 2): project row FOR NO KEY UPDATE (WS:266), new contract NO KEY (WS:444), prior contracts NO KEY plus their exclusive half, then the bound plans read. Plan writers: CreatePlan locks only the audit row (create-plan.ts:55) and then plans.insert (:85); ReviseTarget locks the predecessor plan (revise-plan.ts:60) and then inserts (:118); the control-plane system draft inserts at persistence/src/audit/store.ts:440. None takes the target transition half. The only lock their INSERT takes on the contract is plans_target_fk (0004:42), a KEY SHARE, which conflicts neither with the NO KEY UPDATE of B nor with the advisory half. Interleaving: B reads the plans and sees P1 unaffected; CreatePlan commits P2 on the old contract, binding a value the newer contract lost; B commits keep-current. P2 is then validated, approved (approve-plan.ts:98 sees the old contract current), quoted and paid against a target that no longer accepts the value. The same holds sequentially: after keep-current both contracts are confirmed and current, StartAudit accepts either one (STA:71 checks only confirmed and not superseded), and plans born on the old contract are never compared with the newer one. Line 72 says such a plan "is seen (B waits on its shared half)": plan writers hold no shared half, so the claim is false (checklist 13).
findings.acceptance_criterion: Every writer that binds a plan to a target contract (CreatePlan, ReviseTarget, system draft, and any audit start on it) takes a lock that conflicts with the CMD019 supersession decision, before its own binding, in the documented order. Each writer x CMD019 pair has a RACE cell at that lock, both orders, with a lock-removal control. After a confirmation, at most one contract per project, mode and instance is current, or a later plan birth on the older one is judged against the newer one.
findings.failing_test: T3 "R2-026: RACE CreatePlan binds a plan that uses a lost value while CMD019 reads the bound plans, both orders: the old contract ends superseded, or the plan birth is refused TARGET_STALE"; red with the new writer-side lock removed.

findings.title: Rule 24: the named lock-removal control of the target-reader cells (the explicit exclusive half) leaves them green; no per-reader meeting table; the rebinder and pipeline readers have no cell; the claim that every reader meets B at the shared half is false for EXP and admission
findings.reproduction: M4 says "Fix whose removal turns red: the explicit exclusive half before the plan read". With that half removed, the UPDATE of B still takes the exclusive half through trigger target_contracts_transition_lock (0003:262-264). Each reader holds its shared half to COMMIT (0015:577, 0023:421, 0024:52, WS:405, commerce-subject.ts:90, store.ts:892), so B still waits for it and the outcomes of capture, CreateQuote, ApprovePlan, StartAudit, audits birth and publication are unchanged. Under rule 24 those cells stay green, so they are not C. Their real meeting lock is the await_transition of the reader against the half of the trigger, and the control must remove the await of the reader. Rule 24 also requires a meeting table, actor by actor: the plan gives the trace of B and one sentence for the readers. Census gaps: commerce-subject.ts:85-95 is read by the payments rebinder (apps/api/src/payments/rebinder.ts:63, which issues a re-bound authorization through the 0015 trigger) and by the reconciler (commerce/core/reconciler.ts:78); pipeline.ts:725 (worker authorityAfterLocks) is in the census; none has a cell. Line 68 says every census reader meets B at the target shared half, but EXP meets B at the project row (EXP:56 against WS:266), as the M4 EXP cell itself says, and admission only tries the half (admission.ts:116-121, never waits), so the try cell has no blocked actor.
findings.acceptance_criterion: M4 carries a meeting table: for each reader, every lock in order with file:line and the first lock it shares with CMD019. Each RACE cell names that lock, states the outcome per order, and has a lock-removal control (the await_transition of the reader removed, or the half of B removed where the lock of B is the meeting point) that turns it red. The rebinder, the reconciler subject read and the pipeline publish read each have a cell or a stated reason why they never meet B.
findings.failing_test: For each T3 reader cell, a red-proof variant with the await_transition of the reader removed goes red. "R2-026: RACE the payments rebinder re-binds an authorization while CMD019 supersedes its target, both orders: no ACTIVE authorization on a superseded contract".

findings.title: Rule 15 recurs: five EXPIRY cells hold an earlier await than the last one before the clock read, and CMD019 keeps awaits between its freshness judgment and the UPDATE (ADV-4 partially fixed)
findings.reproduction: Rule 15: "The cell holds that LAST awaited step (not an earlier one)". (1) EXP: the judgment moves after the capacity read EXP:129, but the cell holds the agency half (EXP:101/102); readAuthority :102, agencies.get :105 and capacity :129 follow it, so a clock read placed before :129 stays green. (2) STA: "STA:64 moves after :69", but targetContracts.get at STA:70 is awaited after :69: either an await sits between the judgment and startAudit (:75), or the cell must hold :70. (3) CRT: the cell holds the project row CRT:38, but getArtifact :41 and findLatestForProject :47 come later. (4) SSR, parentless stage: the cell holds the artifact read SSR:59, but hasReceiptFile SSR:67 (and the new reconciliation lookup) come later; the M1 trace (parents right after the stage row) and the P-L1 order (parents after the content-hash check) disagree on which await is last. (5) CTC: the trace is effectNowOf, freshness, bound plans read, targetDriftImpact, UPDATE, and the confirmation-evidence getArtifact at CTC:69 sits after the clock on main: two awaits between the final judgment and the effect.
findings.acceptance_criterion: For each of the 6 judgments (SSR, CST, CTC, CRT, STA, EXP), the plan names the exact statement after which effectNowOf is read, with no await between the judgment and the effect, and the EXPIRY cell holds exactly that last awaited statement (store read or lock) while the deadline crosses. Each cell is red when the clock read moves before that statement.

findings.title: CMD035 issuer revocation cells are unreachable: fiscal_issuers takes its transition lock only on a route_state change, so a numbering, entitlement, legal-fact or validity change never meets the CMD035 shared half
findings.reproduction: M6 REVOCATION: "issuer facts unconfirmed, route SUSPENDED or entitlement withdrawn, numbering authorization changed, each held at its shared half". On 99266f52 fiscal_issuers_transition_lock (0013:489-490) fires only WHEN OLD.route_state IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.route_state. kauro_control holds UPDATE on the whole table (0013:772). An UPDATE that replaces numbering_authorization_ref or entitlement_evidence_hash, moves legal_fact_status from OBSERVED to PROFESSIONALLY_CONFIRMED (or to a value a route accepts), or shortens valid_until, on a QUALIFIED route (CHECK 0013:472-476 still holds), takes no exclusive half. CMD035 holding the issuer shared half does not block it, so CMD035 submits under the old numbering or entitlement, judged on a stale row. L0D (0074) changes only tax_documents. Only route SUSPENDED is reachable as written. Rule 16: the judged authority must sit under a lock that conflicts with its revoker.
findings.acceptance_criterion: Every fiscal_issuers column CMD035 judges (route_state, legal_fact_status, numbering_authorization_ref, entitlement_evidence_hash, valid_from, valid_until, qualification_evidence_hashes) is changed only under the exclusive half of the issuer, and CMD035 judges them from a row read after its shared half in the same transaction. Each column has a REVOCATION cell where the writer is blocked by CMD035, or commits first and is seen, both orders, red with the widened trigger removed.

findings.title: CMD035 intent EXPIRY is marked N/A although the issuer route validity, the numbering authorization validity and the profile validity bound the issuance
findings.reproduction: M6 intent row: "N/A at intent (the deadline is born here)". fiscal_issuers carries valid_from/valid_until (0013:468-469) and fiscal_profiles carries validity (commerce-platform.ts:178-179 validFrom/validUntil). The 0017:163 validation guard judges the profile only at the tax point of the sale, not at the issuance instant. A DIAN numbering resolution has a validity window. An issuer whose valid_until passes while CMD035 waits on the document row is still submitted, because nothing judges it at effect_now after the last lock. Rule 23: an instant that bounds an authority window is judged at the database clock.

An EXPIRY cell crosses valid_until while CMD035 waits on the document row and on its exclusive half (the last await): nothing is submitted.

findings.title: The credit-note race cell is held at the invoice row, a lock drafting never takes in a conflicting mode (unreachable as titled); the invoice-before-credit-note order of the CMD035 conclusion is not placed

findings.title: The L7 TARGET-REBIND deferral (the included repair of R2-026) has no package, date or blocking dependency, and the product view hard-codes repair NOT_AVAILABLE_V1, a V1 cut of an R2 MUST
findings.reproduction: R2-026 expects "provide included repair/refund/new-scope paths without an automatic extra charge". Section 7 is titled "nothing designed against a moving interface", but it gives no moving interface, owner, date or package for L7. replacement.ts is in no in-flight worktree diff (measured over repos/* against 99266f52), so nothing blocks it. P-L1 builds the view literal repair: NOT_AVAILABLE_V1, and CV-11 accepts that a paid ACTIVE authorization stays unexecutable until L7. With ADV-21 applied, every CRM contract change strands paid entitlements, so L7 is on the B17 close path. The deferral therefore hides a MUST: CLAUDE.md section 0 says full scope, no cuts.
findings.acceptance_criterion: L7 is a scheduled lane of this plan (files, matrix before code, cells, order) or a named package with a date before B17 close. R2-026 stays PART in the case map until L7 is C. No product view or contract carries a V1-unavailable literal for an R2-required path.

findings.title: The S078 qualification gate is not scoped by mode: CMD058 also versions CLEAN capabilities (no importer tool, no export-back), so the CV-8 statement that every CMD058 blocks until D-12 silently disables a command that works on main
findings.reproduction: change-capability.ts:40-65 versions any capability in a versionable state, whatever its mode. M5 adds five predicates to every call: the ref resolves in vendor_qualifications (which has no producer and no runtime INSERT grant), tool equals the profile tool, profileHash, PASS, and exportBackHash non-null. A CLEAN capability has no importer tool and no export-back, so its versions are refused once L4 lands. That blocks a CLEAN-only launch path on D-12, a Salesforce/HubSpot owner act unrelated to CLEAN. CV-8 calls this "the conservative reading, not a defect". S078 (05:69) concerns importer workflows, not CLEAN.
findings.acceptance_criterion: The S078 predicates apply to the CRM-mode capabilities whose profile names an importer tool. CLEAN capability versions keep their main-line behaviour (or a stated CLEAN qualification rule with its R2 source). An OK sibling proves a CLEAN version records with no vendor qualification. CV-8 states the exact set of capabilities blocked until D-12.
findings.failing_test: T4 "S078: OK a CLEAN capability version records without a vendor qualification"; it goes red with the unscoped gate.
